title: Sherlock Holmes: A Study in Scarlet — Ep 08/14 — "On the Great Alkali Plain"
description:
A Study in Scarlet, Episode 8. London is a long way behind us. This one begins in a desert, thirty-four years earlier.

On the fourth of May, 1847, a man stood on the northern slope of the Sierra Blanco and looked for water. He was one of twenty-one; the rest were dead behind him. The bundle he set down off his shoulder was a child of five in a pink frock somebody had kept clean, and he had been three days finding a way to tell her that her mother was not coming.

She took it better than he did. If they were dying, she said, then they were only going to where her mother already was.

Three specks came up out of the north and settled on the ledge above them, and she clapped to make them fly.

Then the far edge of the plain began to smoke — ten thousand people coming west with their waggons and their oxen and their guns — and the man who led them offered water on one condition.

This is where the other half of the story starts. Everything in London follows from it.

Chapter I of Part Two of Arthur Conan Doyle's A Study in Scarlet (1887), in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
